name: AI-First Customer Success Showcase
description: A DevRev PLuG + Turing AI showcase environment for prospects evaluating DevRev as an AI-native support platform. Demonstrates: AI-deflection on common questions via PLuG, Turing-powered ticket triage and auto-routing, AI-generated KB article suggestions, sentiment-based escalation, and the full omnichannel loop (email, chat, Slack). Designed for a modern SaaS company ('Velo Analytics') with a realistic product hierarchy and a mix of low-complexity deflectable tickets and high-severity escalations that show what the AI escalates vs. handles autonomously.

plug_config.welcome_message: Hi there! I'm Velo's AI support assistant. Ask me anything — I can usually answer instantly. If not, I'll connect you with a human right away.
plug_config.ai_grounding_notes: You are Velo Analytics' AI support assistant. Velo is a B2B SaaS analytics platform used by data teams. Users are typically data analysts, data engineers, or business intelligence managers. Common questions: connecting data sources, pipeline failures, dashboard sharing, billing/seat management, and API quota errors. Always check KB articles before escalating. For billing questions, route to the billing team. For data pipeline outages, escalate immediately to p0. Do not share internal pricing tiers or contractual information — route those to the sales team.

works.title: How do I share a dashboard with an external stakeholder?
works.body: User asked via PLuG chat: 'Can I share a dashboard with someone who doesn't have a Velo login?' AI identified the KB article on public embed links and shared it. User confirmed resolved without human intervention. Demonstrates: AI deflection of tier-1 how-to question.

works.title: Snowflake connector failing — authentication error after credential rotation
works.body: Pipeline to Snowflake stopped syncing after the customer rotated their service account credentials. AI identified the root cause from the error message, walked the user through the re-authentication steps in the connector settings, and confirmed the pipeline resumed. Zero human involvement. Demonstrates: AI-driven connector troubleshooting.

works.title: Anomaly detection firing false positives on weekend traffic
works.body: Prism Health user reporting that the anomaly detection model is triggering alerts every Saturday night on expected low-traffic patterns. AI recognized this as a known sensitivity threshold issue, explained how to set business-hours-only alert windows, and linked the KB article. User confirmed the issue is resolved. Demonstrates: AI explaining product behavior and resolving configuration questions.

works.title: CRITICAL: entire Northstar data pipeline down — no data since 14:00 UTC
works.body: All Northstar Retail pipelines stopped processing at 14:00 UTC. Dashboards showing stale data. 180 users affected. AI detected the severity from keyword analysis ('entire', 'no data', 'critical'), performed negative sentiment scoring on the message tone, and immediately escalated to the Data Engineering Support group with full context. No AI resolution attempted. Demonstrates: AI knowing when NOT to handle something — immediate human escalation for outages with churn-risk accounts.

works.title: API quota limit hit — unable to run forecasting jobs
works.body: FiveX Capital data team hitting the API rate limit on the forecasting endpoint. AI identified the account tier (Growth, 10k calls/day limit) and explained how to batch requests, optimize call frequency, and request a temporary quota increase. Also flagged the account for a proactive CSM outreach given repeated quota hits. Demonstrates: AI handling quota questions + triggering CSM workflow.

works.title: Need to add 10 seats for new data team — how does billing work?
works.body: Northstar IT admin asking about adding seats mid-cycle. AI recognized a billing/contract question, declined to provide pricing details, and routed to the Billing & Ops team with the account context pre-filled. Demonstrates: AI correctly scoping its own limits and routing to the right human queue.

works.title: SSO login broken after Okta configuration change
works.body: Prism Health users unable to log in after their IT team updated the Okta SAML configuration. AI walked the user through the SAML attribute mapping checklist, identified the mismatched NameID format, and resolved the issue without escalation. Demonstrates: AI resolving complex SSO configuration issues from KB knowledge.

works.title: User expressing frustration — 'This is the third time this month my pipeline has broken'
works.body: Northstar user Lena Marchetti sent a message expressing strong frustration about recurring pipeline instability. AI performed sentiment analysis, flagged the ticket as negative sentiment and churn-risk, and immediately routed to Customer Success with an alert. CSM was notified within 90 seconds. Demonstrates: AI sentiment detection triggering proactive CSM intervention before a customer churns.

articles.title: Sharing Dashboards — Public Links, Embeds, and Guest Access
articles.body: How to share a Velo dashboard with external stakeholders who don't have a Velo login: generate a public read-only link, embed a dashboard in an external site via iframe, or invite a guest user. Permissions model explained.

articles.title: Snowflake Connector — Re-authenticating After Credential Rotation
articles.body: Step-by-step: navigate to Integrations → Snowflake → Edit credentials. Paste the new service account private key or password. Click Test Connection. If authentication still fails, check that the Snowflake role has USAGE on the target warehouse and database.

articles.title: Anomaly Detection — Tuning Sensitivity and Business Hours Filtering
articles.body: How to reduce false positives: adjust the sensitivity slider in AI Insights → Anomaly Settings. Enable Business Hours mode to suppress alerts outside your team's working hours. Explanation of the z-score threshold and how seasonal patterns are learned.

articles.title: API Rate Limits — Understanding Quotas and Requesting Increases
articles.body: Velo API rate limits by plan tier: Starter (1k/day), Growth (10k/day), Enterprise (unlimited). How to batch forecast requests. How to monitor quota usage via the API dashboard. How to request a temporary quota increase via support.

articles.title: SSO Setup — SAML 2.0 Configuration with Okta, Azure AD, and Google Workspace
articles.body: Complete SAML configuration guide for the three major IdPs. Common errors: NameID format mismatch, attribute mapping issues, clock skew. Troubleshooting checklist for broken SSO logins. How to test SAML assertions with your browser's network inspector.

articles.title: Data Pipeline Failures — First-Response Triage Guide
articles.body: How to diagnose a pipeline failure in under 5 minutes: check the job run log for error codes, common causes (credentials expired, schema drift, warehouse timeout, network issues), and how to trigger a manual re-run. When to escalate to DevRev support.

articles.title: How Velo Uses DevRev AI to Deflect 60%+ of Support Tickets
articles.body: Internal SE resource: overview of how the PLuG AI agent is configured for Velo Analytics. KB grounding strategy, escalation rules, sentiment detection, and CSM trigger setup. Use this in demos to explain the AI-first support model.

articles.title: Turing AI Triage — How Automatic Routing and Summarization Work
articles.body: How DevRev Turing automatically classifies incoming tickets, suggests KB articles, routes to the right group, and generates conversation summaries for human agents. Configuration options in Settings → AI → Triage.

articles.body: How DevRev's sentiment analysis flags at-risk customers, triggers CSM alerts, and feeds the churn-risk signal. How to configure escalation rules in Settings → AI → Sentiment Escalation. Worked examples from Velo's support team.

ui_guidance.title: PLuG AI widget — what to demo first
steps: Open the PLuG widget in the demo org and ask: 'How do I share a dashboard?' — AI instantly cites the KB article and resolves without human.
Then ask: 'My entire data pipeline is down and I've lost two hours of data' — AI detects the severity and escalates immediately. Show the contrast.
Then express frustration: 'This is the third time this month my pipeline has broken' — Turing flags negative sentiment and triggers the CSM alert. Show the timeline_entry AI annotation on the ticket.
This three-step flow — deflect, escalate, sentiment — is the core of the AI-first story in 5 minutes.

ui_guidance.title: Configuring the PLuG AI agent
steps: Go to Settings → PLuG → AI Agent to view and edit the grounding notes in this blueprint.
The ai_grounding_notes field tells Turing what the product is, who the users are, what to answer, and critically — what NOT to answer (billing, pricing, contract terms).
Connect KB articles to the AI agent under Settings → PLuG → Knowledge Base. Published articles in this blueprint are automatically eligible for AI grounding.
Test grounding quality using the Preview mode before going live.
Adjust tone, fallback behavior, and human handoff triggers under Settings → PLuG → Escalation Rules.

ui_guidance.title: Turing AI triage — auto-routing and summarization
steps: Turing automatically classifies every incoming ticket by product area, priority, and intent — no manual tagging needed.
Routing rules are configured under Settings → AI → Triage. For this showcase, tickets with 'pipeline' or 'connector' keywords route to the Data Engineering Support group.
Billing questions route to Billing & Ops. Sentiment-negative tickets route to Customer Success.
Turing generates a 2-3 sentence summary on every ticket so human agents have instant context when they pick up an escalation.
Show the 'AI Triage Queue' group in the demo — every ticket that arrives here has been pre-classified and summarized before a human sees it.

ui_guidance.title: Sentiment detection and churn-risk escalation
steps: Turing scores every message for sentiment. Scores below -0.7 trigger the 'sentiment-negative' tag and a CSM alert.
The 'churn-risk' tag is applied when: (a) sentiment is negative AND (b) the account has had 2+ P0/P1 tickets in the last 30 days.
Configure escalation rules under Settings → AI → Sentiment Escalation. Set the threshold, the team to notify, and the escalation message.
In the demo, show work:t08 (Lena Marchetti's frustration ticket) — the internal timeline entry shows the AI scoring and the automatic CSM notification firing within 90 seconds.
Emphasize: the CSM was notified before any human support agent even saw the ticket. This is proactive retention, not reactive firefighting.

ui_guidance.title: AI-generated KB article suggestions
steps: When AI cannot fully resolve a ticket, it suggests the top 3 matching KB articles for the agent to review and share.
Agents can push a KB article directly to the customer from within the ticket — no copy-paste.
If the AI suggestion resolved the ticket, mark it 'AI Resolved' and tag it 'ai-suggested-article'. This feeds the deflection rate metric.
Use Settings → AI → Knowledge Gaps to see which tickets had no matching article — these are gaps in your KB that should be filled.
For the demo: show the AI article suggestion panel on work:t02 (Snowflake auth error) — the AI matched the re-authentication article at 0.94 confidence.

ui_guidance.title: Custom stages for the AI workflow
steps: This blueprint adds four custom stages to complement DevRev's built-in pipeline.
'AI Handling' (ordinal 150) — ticket is being worked by the AI agent. No human has seen it yet.
'Awaiting User' (ordinal 350) — AI asked a clarifying question; waiting for the customer to respond.
'Escalated to Human' (ordinal 450) — AI determined it cannot resolve this and handed off to a human agent.
'AI Resolved' (closed, ordinal 750) — AI resolved the ticket autonomously. Tracked separately from human-resolved for deflection metrics.
Go to Settings → Object Customization → Stage Diagrams to configure the allowed transitions and set up automation rules that move tickets between AI Handling and Escalated to Human.

ui_guidance.title: Measuring AI deflection rate
steps: Deflection rate = tickets tagged 'ai-deflected' / total tickets in period. Target: 60%+ for mature AI-grounded orgs.
Track in DevRev Insights: create a metric filtering tickets by the 'ai-deflected' tag and trending over time.
Mean time to resolution (MTTR) for AI-resolved tickets vs. human-resolved tickets shows the velocity improvement.
Knowledge Gap report (Settings → AI → Knowledge Gaps) shows which categories need more KB articles to improve deflection.
During the demo, show that deflection isn't just about cost savings — it's faster for the customer (seconds vs. hours) and frees human agents for the complex, high-value conversations.
